title: Is taking away a negative number the same as adding?
description: Three take aways of a negative number from the lift work are placed beside the matching sums with a positive number. Each pair gives the same answer, so the pattern is named. Keeko's doubt is that subtracting always makes a number smaller.
teaching_notes: One idea: taking away a negative number gives the same answer as adding the matching positive number. Watch for students who believe subtracting always makes a number smaller, even when the lift starts below the ground.

source: In the other exercises that you did above, did you notice th
video_script.why: The child sees from the lift that taking away a negative number gives the same answer as adding the matching positive number.
video_script.substitution: Three take aways of a negative number from the book's lift work, each placed beside its matching sum.
video_script.anchor: the mine lift and the infinite lift, with each take away beside its matching sum
video_script.wrong_answer: subtracting always makes a number smaller
video_script.wrong_move: believes a take away must give a smaller number, so taking away a negative cannot match adding
video_script.payoff_line: Taking away a negative number is the same as adding the matching positive number.

final_answer.value: Yes, subtracting a negative number is the same as adding the corresponding positive number
final_answer.spoken: yes, taking away a negative number is the same as adding the matching positive number

hold_back: Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding the corresponding positive number
maths_rules: slip: 90 is bigger than 40, so this take away did not make the number smaller
video_script.design: Three rows, each a take away on the lift with the matching sum written beside it; the rows are laid out so the matching answers line up.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the mine lift going from level -50 up to level +40

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the mine lift is drawn
marks.mine: the lift climbs from level -50 to level +40 and (+40) - (-50) = +90 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about taking away and adding.
<bookmark mark='mine'/>In the mine, taking away negative fifty from positive forty gave ninety.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Does positive forty plus positive fifty give ninety too?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: Target level - Starting level = Movement needed; x - (-y) beside x + (+y)

marks.rule: the line Target level - Starting level = Movement needed is written
marks.below: a lift starting below the ground is drawn, with an arrow up

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>In a take away, the first level is the target, and the second level is the start.
<bookmark mark='below'/>When the second level is negative, the lift starts below the ground and has to climb.

marks.given: the three take aways from the lift work are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three take aways from the lift work, each of a negative number.

beats.on_screen: To find: is each the same as adding the matching positive number?
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to see whether each one is the same as adding the matching positive number.

marks.m1: the lift climbs 50 to the ground and 40 more, and +90 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, positive forty take away negative fifty.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>The lift climbs fifty to the ground and forty more, so ninety.
<bookmark mark='p1'/>Positive forty plus positive fifty is ninety too.

marks.m2: the lift climbs 55 to the ground and 105 more, and +160 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, positive one hundred five take away negative fifty five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The lift climbs fifty five to the ground and one hundred five more, so one hundred sixty.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>Positive one hundred five plus positive fifty five is one hundred sixty too.

marks.m3: the lift climbs 200 to the ground and 2000 more, and +2200 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, positive two thousand take away negative two hundred.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The lift climbs two hundred to the ground and two thousand more, so two thousand two hundred.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>Positive two thousand plus positive two hundred is two thousand two hundred too.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Yes. Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding the corresponding positive number

marks.match: the three pairs of equal answers are joined
marks.pay: the sentence is written and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='match'/>In every pair, the two answers match.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Taking away a negative number is the same as adding the matching positive number.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: +90 above +40 on the shaft with an arrow rising from level -50; smaller crossed out

marks.fix: the words are struck out and 90 is marked above 40 on the shaft
marks.why: the arrow from level -50 to level +40 lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks subtracting always makes a number smaller, so it cannot match adding.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the answer ninety is bigger than forty.
<bookmark mark='why'/>The lift starts below the ground, so taking away a negative number makes it climb.
